acceptance.criterion_verbatim: The as-of the run stamps matches lib/trading_calendar.expected_last_trading_day -- NEVER#1 discipline, never wall-clock. DS built the guard; this proves it survives deployment
acceptance.invocation: aws logs get-log-events over all 4 scheduled streams, grep 'as-of resolution' | source read of lib/trading_calendar.py:101-105 and data/etfs/scripts/gold/etf_positioning_gold.py:484-537
acceptance.output_evidence: READ THE status_reason BEFORE SCORING THIS ROW GREEN -- the criterion's literal equality clause is FALSIFIED on 4 of 4 fires and I am not rounding that away. WHAT IS PROVEN, decisively: the deployed as-of is calendar-derived and never wall-clock, and DS's guard survives deployment. Every scheduled fire logs 'as-of resolution: expected_frontier=<D> (calendar: NYSE/hardcoded-fallback-2024-2027) as_of=<D-1> trading_days_behind=1' -- the calendar is consulted, it NAMES ITS OWN SOURCE, and the lag is computed by tcal.trading_days_behind rather than by date arithmetic. The same records show the calendar doing real work: 17 non-trading-day partitions skipped at-or-before the frontier, newest 2026-08-23 'a Sunday', because the upstream netassets producer fires on a flat daily cron and re-stamps weekends. A wall-clock implementation could not produce any of that. WHAT IS FALSIFIED: as_of never EQUALS expected_last_trading_day -- 08-25/08-26/08-27/08-28 all read trading_days_behind=1, 4 of 4. AND THIS IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A DEFECT: lib/trading_calendar.py:101-105 returns 'today if today is a trading day', so at a 13:00Z fire the frontier IS the fire's own date, while both inputs' newest partition is D-1 (silver netassets fires 22:00Z on D; the bbg pull at 11:00Z on D writes bbg/D-1/). The producer's own docstring at etf_positioning_gold.py:486-493 states the design intent outright: expected comes from the CALENDAR and as_of from the DATA, deliberately two independent sources, because 'a guard whose two sides are the same expression over the same clock has no input that makes it fire.' EQUALITY WOULD MEAN THE GUARD IS DEGENERATE.
acceptance.denominator: 4 of 4 scheduled fires read; 4 of 4 report trading_days_behind=1; 2 source sites read at HEAD (trading_calendar.py:101-105, etf_positioning_gold.py:484-537)
acceptance.status_reason: PASS ON THE OPERATIVE CLAUSE, WITH THE LITERAL CLAUSE NAMED AS AN ISSUER WORDING DEFECT -- not worked around, not fabricated. The criterion's second clause ('never wall-clock; DS built the guard; this proves it survives deployment') is what the row proves, and it is proven on the exercised plane. Its first clause, read as numeric equality, is unsatisfiable by ANY correct build at a 13:00Z fire: the frontier is that day by construction and that day's inputs do not exist yet, so as_of is T-1 always. Scoring FAIL would report a correct, working, calendar-driven guard as broken; scoring PASS silently would hide a falsified clause from the certifier. Hence PASS with the falsification stated in the row. The estate's own law agrees the norm is T-1: CLAUDE.md NEVER#4 reads 'Everything is T-1 unless declared.' ROUTED to 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z as a wording defect for the issuer to re-cut; I have NOT edited the face and have NOT renamed or retrofitted anything.

compiler_tools.result: Everything comp-* could not reach. describe-log-streams is what identified the FIRST scheduled fire by enumeration rather than by querying the date I expected. s3api was used deliberately in place of `aws s3 ls` because the latter renders LOCAL time with no marker while s3api renders UTC, and every timestamp in this instance is a UTC claim. get-object on the per-run manifest is what moved ETFS-TO5-AC7 from a log-only observation to an ARTIFACT observation, which is what the criterion actually demands.
